paper.central_claim: A bi-level multi-agent system (orchestrator + parallel workers on a shared workboard) jointly evolves decomposition skills and execution skills through a run-verify-reflect loop over external memory (no weight updates), reaching SOTA on WideSearch (Avg@4 SR 38.50, Row F1 63.53, Item F1 80.12) and 73.0 on XBench-DeepSearch.
paper.title: Web2BigTable: A Bi-Level Multi-Agent LLM System for Internet-Scale Information Search and Extraction

gap.author_gap: Web-to-table (wide) search needs broad, consistent coverage; monolithic agents saturate context, and hierarchical/workflow-search frameworks use fixed or weakly adaptive decomposition with little feedback from execution to decomposition; self-evolving agents adapt at only one level.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete and demonstrated: case studies show default time-window decomposition mixes tours/product lines and causes coverage failure (234 of 534 rows retrieved), which the learned skill fixes. The learned object (decomposition strategy) is clearly distinct from evolved execution skills. Nearest neighbours (automated workflow search, Memento-Skills, SAGE, SkillRL, G-Memory) are named but not compared experimentally; the only learned-decomposition comparator is the authors' own no-skill ablation.
gap.lineage: ReAct/deep research agents -> hierarchical multi-agent decomposition and automated workflow search (AFlow-like) -> skill-library self-evolving agents (Memento-Skills, SAGE) -> bi-level decomposition+execution skill learning with shared workboard.
gap.closest_adjacent: Memento-Skills (supplies the worker agent), automated workflow search, EvolveR/SAMULE reflection; none run as baselines.
gap.residue: Learning how to decompose (which axis to split a wide task on) from gold-referenced failures, rather than hand-set heuristics.
gap.stakes: WideSearch success rates of 0-5% for all prior systems (author table).
gap.method_response: Reflect over failure clusters into router + decomposition skills; shared workboard for coordination.
gap.remaining_gap: Whether a hand-written decomposition skill gives the same gain; transfer of learned skills across benchmarks; label-free (no gold) skill learning; cost.
gap.unresolved: Head-to-head with learned-decomposition neighbours; role of benchmark-specific training queries.

rs_pattern.reason: Opus sides with son55. Decomposition is the paper's central object: the orchestrator partitions a wide query into entity/source/category subtasks with a typed result schema and tag-partitioned slots (C25 lists a 'typed inter-agent deliverable'), the loop is closed at training by gold-table Item-F1, and the store-off ablation collapses the system toward the generic-decomposition baseline (C25 step 4). The delegated solver is a worker-agent pool, not a symbolic solver, so fit is partial on step 1. adapt_via_conditioning (sub null) supports: the learned SKILL.md banks are read as in-context conditioning of frozen LLMs. sol's adapt_via_conditioning-only reading misses the decomposition that the method learns.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Step 1 (name the structural cause: static decomposition causing coverage gaps) executed with case studies; step 2 (typed schema-conforming slots) executed; step 3 (close loop with verifiable signal) executed at training via gold-table Item-F1 (privileged, disclosed); step 4 (ablate the load-bearing mechanism: collapse to baseline) executed for learned orchestrator skills; step 5 (cost of delegation, other benchmarks) cost not reported, two benchmarks only.
matches.success_failure_checks: Success: single load-bearing mechanism isolated by ablation; intermediate by-products accumulated as reusable capital. Failure: off-the-shelf components (Memento-Skills workers, GPT-5 mini) with cost unmeasured; benchmark-specific skills.
matches.reason: Delegated solver here is a worker agent pool rather than a symbolic solver, but the artifact, closed-loop verification and ablation conditions are met.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Learned SKILL.md bank is read as in-context conditioning of frozen LLMs; C03 category-holdout, contamination audit and cheaper-conditioning baseline not executed.
matches.success_failure_checks: No contamination audit between synthesised training queries and test tasks; no longer-context/hand-written-skill baseline.
matches.reason: Secondary: describes how the learned state is consumed at inference.

Versioned SKILL.md packages (human-editable) yes; mined from many sources and quality/execution gate no; reuse evaluated on tasks disjoint from training only through perturbed benchmark queries.
Worker SkillCreator/self-repair with AST validation and indexing matches forge+repair loop; reuse on held-out tasks not isolated; forging is buried inside a larger architecture (F1).

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported: decomposition skills learned once from 20 benchmark-derived gold-referenced queries and frozen produced a large held-out gain over the same system with generic decomposition (WideSearch SR 7.0 -> 38.5; XBench 41.0 -> 73.0). Not shown: independence from the training-test template overlap, transfer across benchmarks, improver level, matched cost, or that worker-skill evolution (vs catalogue use) matters.
unresolved: Contamination of perturbed training queries; hand-written-skill baseline; cost; variance of skill learning; worker-evolution isolation.
Opus: displayed learned skills encode test-task entities/columns (opus:O01–O05); held-out status of the gain is weaker than 'unmodified test set' suggests.
Opus: test-time skill creation/repair contradicts the frozen-inference description (opus:O06).

G.reason: Opus sides with son55. The bottleneck (a fixed decomposition axis leaves coverage gaps in wide search; context saturation of monolithic agents) is concrete and directly exhibited by the generic-decomposition arm and case studies. The lineage is explicit: workers are Memento-Skills agents, and the delta is the orchestrator-level skill learning plus the workboard; single-level self-evolving skill agents are named with the difference stated. Not 4: the residual against automatically searched workflows, which also learn decomposition from execution, is asserted ('fixed or weakly adaptive') rather than contrasted.

M.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Gold-verified error reports, clustering by structural decomposition pattern, per-cluster skill synthesis and a router skill form a reconstructible response to the coverage gap. Not 4: no argument why learned skills should beat a hand-written decomposition prompt, and the worker-level rationale is thin.

X.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Training/inference split, router and workboard locking are clear. Retention is append-only with no gate, conflict handling or forgetting; bank size is unreported; and the description contradicts itself (read-only inference vs runtime skill creation, opus:O06; 'no deduplication' vs deduplicated case studies; single pass vs Round 2).

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Established benchmarks with strict SR plus row/item F1 against gold tables. Concerns: LLM judgement for free-text cells and XBench, and baselines taken from published reports (comparability is charged in E.causality).

E.causality.reason: Opus sides with sol. The store-off ablation of the retained orchestrator skills (same system, both benchmarks) and same-backbone single agents are the key controls, and they are large. But the strongest alternative for the RSI claim — decomposition skills written without feedback (hand-written, or one LLM pass) — is untested, the 'generic' decomposition arm is a weak default, baselines are not budget- or backbone-matched (10 workers, 8,000 cloud skills), and the worker-evolution arm also removes catalogue discovery. Run convention: store-off without an alternative-optimizer or budget-matched arm = 2 (r11b EvoSkill, r15a CoEvoSkills); MineEvolve's 3 had matched alternative stores.

E.holdout.reason: Shared correction 2 → 1. Frozen skills evaluated on the unmodified benchmark is the right design, but training queries are parameter perturbations of benchmark tasks (opus:O05), and the paper's own displayed learned skills encode specific test tasks: AMD product lines and a cache/GPU worker for ws_en_091 (opus:O01–O03), an arXiv-date rule for ws_zh_069 (opus:O04). The 'structural placeholders only' safeguard is contradicted, no overlap audit exists, skills are learned per benchmark, and test-time skill creation persists (opus:O06).

E.statistics.reason: Opus sides with sol (A2 ladder; r15a SkillX precedent). Avg@4 and Max@4 average four inference runs into point estimates with no dispersion, interval or test, from a single skill-learning run; XBench is a single run with 1-point margins.

E.cost.reason: Both seats not_reported. 'Cost-efficient' models are asserted, but no tokens, calls, wall-clock, dollars or training-phase cost are reported for 10 parallel workers, reflection LLMs and skill retrieval.
